item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00430","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C06","C23","C08"],"selected_candidate_label":"C06","confidence":0.78,"relationship_type":"literal_language_template","rationale":"C06 plausibly supplied a material rhetorical and drafting template: both letters announce a policy favoring the fullest practicable public disclosure, immediately qualify that policy by national-interest or national-security constraints, and distinguish withholding protected material from withholding releasable facts. C23 contains essentially the same formulation but expressly identifies itself as following the earlier C06 response, making C06 the stronger antecedent. C08 is relevant to the same disclosure-versus-security balance but is a detailed classification order whose operative machinery is not reproduced in the child.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"It is the policy of this Administration to unfold the historical record as fast and as fully as is consistent with national security and with friendly relations with foreign nations.","parent_excerpt":"it is the established policy of the Executive Branch to provide the Congress and the public with the fullest possible information consistent with the national interest.","explanation":"The two letters use a closely parallel policy formula: maximum disclosure qualified by security or national-interest limits."},{"child_excerpt":"because of the inherent need for security in the current conduct of foreign affairs, it is obviously not possible to make full immediate disclosure of diplomatic papers. However, delay in such disclosure must be kept to a minimum.","parent_excerpt":"Although I have forbidden the furnishing of the evaluation report requested by you, I wish to make it clear that this has not been done for the purpose of preventing the disclosure of any facts shown by the report. Such facts will be made available to you as promptly as possible.","explanation":"Both qualify nondisclosure narrowly and emphasize prompt release of information that can properly be disclosed."},{"child_excerpt":"any official should have a clear and precise case involving the national interest before seeking to withhold from publication documents or papers fifteen or more years old.","parent_excerpt":"The President has throughout our history, in compliance with his duty in this regard, withheld information when he found that the disclosure of what was sought would be incompatible with the national interest.","explanation":"Both frame withholding executive documents as requiring a specific national-interest justification."}]}
